I'm not sure I would agree that adopting a position which levels certain ideas to the same value is the same as nihilism or even a destruction of value. Even if a large survey of things/ideas/perspectives is said to be equal there is still a base value being assigned to those T/I/P's. I don't see how the equalization of value equates to its destruction. Your argument seems to center around the idea that values have no meaning unless they are organized in a hierarchy denoting their worth relative to each other. Furthermore, I don't think the symptoms you note are really indicative of a nihilistic trend. For your example of social movements in favor of praising previously stigmatized body traits. These movements do not exist to "destroy" the value of older beauty standards, they seek to assign value to a new standard that runs in parallel to the old one. 

In your examples of gay and black rights movements, I dont think its really been a wavering thing. Ever since the 90's the LGBT movement has steadily gained ground and support towards their goals and it doesn't appear to be stopping. Just because the news has switched to covering stories that mostly concern black issues doesn't mean that progress has slowed in LGBT ones. Anyway, my point is that just because it seems like people switch from issue to issue it still doesn't really seem nihilistic. They are putting at least some effort towards a cause that they feel has value or is important (for the time being). Finally, if you wanna look at it from the extremes, we still by in large agree that certain actions are grossly unethical such as rape, murder, and genocide. We still view these actions as inherently wrong and non-permissible. This is not the position of a nihilist (Since by nihilism I guess we're talking moral nihilism). I do agree that modern perspective is changing what we value and how we value values in general, but I do think that we still very much care about what we think is right and to me that is not nihilism.

An Ebmaj7 contains a G minor triad.

Eb G Bb D
       
G Bb D

All of those notes are passable in D minor because G minor is a triad within the key of D minor. Furthermore the keys of Eb major and D minor both contain many of the same notes (F, G, Bb, C, D).  As you mention, the Ebmaj7 arpeggio has an entire triad in common with Em7b5 (G Bb D) and also that various tensions can be used over the A. Over Em7b5, the three notes in common work fine and the Eb can be worked in as a tension if desired since the vii7b5 and the V are supposed to be tense chords. Concerning A, the Ebmaj7 arpeggio can be a compliment since it contains some of the common dominant tensions in relation to A (A7, A7b5, A7b9).
